study_text: I have an interdisciplinary background in social science and computer science. I am interested in the influence of current AI on society (positive and negative), and in how AI can be used to benefit society and enable humans rather than replace them.
work_text: My professional career is currently focused on cloud deployment and DevOps. My interest here is to ensure secure, stable deployments that are EU-law compliant and tailored to the customers' wishes.
life_text: I focus on AI and data science, spanning the full pipeline from organising and modelling client data to analysing it for insights or building models based on it. I have researched the robustness and explainability of deep-learning-based models across various domains.

blog_description: Personal notes about ideas worth developing in my own words.
blog_post_why_title: Why I Am Starting a Blog in the Age of AI
blog_post_why_excerpt: AI can generate polished text in seconds. That makes the slow and imperfect work of forming our own thoughts more important, not less.
blog_post_why_body_1: Writing has never only been a way to present finished ideas. It is one of the ways I discover what I actually think. A vague intuition has to survive questions, structure, and revision before it becomes an argument I can stand behind.
blog_post_why_body_2: Generative AI makes it easy to skip that process. It can produce a plausible answer, a clean summary, or a confident opinion before I have spent time with the question myself. This is useful, but it also creates the temptation to mistake fluent language for understanding.
blog_post_why_body_3: I do not want to reject AI. I work with it and remain fascinated by what it can enable. But I want to preserve spaces in which efficiency is not the only goal. Human judgment, curiosity, doubt, and lived experience matter precisely because they cannot be reduced to predicting the next convincing sentence.
blog_post_why_body_4: This blog is one of those spaces. It gives me a reason to slow down, follow an idea beyond its first formulation, and make my assumptions visible. Publishing also adds useful responsibility: if a thought is worth sharing, it should be clear enough to question and specific enough to be wrong.
blog_post_why_body_5: The posts here will therefore be written to develop my thinking, not merely to fill a page. AI may help me research, challenge, or edit, but it should not replace the act of deciding what I believe and why. In an age of abundant generated content, that act feels more valuable than ever.
